title: Collect the record on SBD-SYSLOG01
subtitle: Design the logging pipeline and build its collector
description: The first of three logging courses: design the whole collect → protect → analyze pipeline, then build its first stage — advanced audit policy on the DCs and admin hosts, source-initiated Windows Event Forwarding and a syslog intake on SBD-SYSLOG01, health checks with a named owner, and proof that real events arrive with the right names and times.
outcomes: Design all three logging stages: retention, readers, streams, and register rows.
Write the designed audit events on the DCs and admin hosts through GPO.
Forward Windows events by source-initiated subscription and take syslog from the router and SBD-REPO01.
Keep the collector healthy and prove collection with events you cause.

stages.title: Design collect, protect, analyze
stages.detail: Three systems, three distinct jobs: SBD-SYSLOG01 gathers, SBD-AUDIT01 preserves, SBD-SPLUNK01 answers questions. This course builds the first; courses 1.11 and 1.12 build the other two — so decide now, for all three, what is collected, how long it lives, who may touch it, and where each stream is picked up.

stages.title: Turn on the right auditing
stages.detail: Forwarding garbage faster is not monitoring. Set the advanced audit policy so the events that tell the network's story — sign-ins, account changes, directory changes, policy changes — actually get written, at or above the STIG values course 1.4 measured.

stages.title: Build the collector
stages.detail: SBD-SYSLOG01 becomes the funnel: Windows Event Forwarding brings the DC and admin-host events in by source-initiated subscription, and a syslog receiver takes the core router's denies and, from the next lessons, the Linux servers over TLS — one host where the network's record first lands.

stages.title: Keep the collector trustworthy
stages.detail: A collector that silently stops is worse than none, because everyone assumes it works. Watch the subscription's runtime status, the sources that went quiet, the log's size and overwrite behavior, the disk, and the syslog intake — and decide who is told when collection fails.

stages.title: Prove collection and hand off
stages.detail: Prove the collector with events you cause on purpose: a failed sign-in, a denied probe, and a test message from SBD-REPO01, the first Linux source. Each must land with the right source name and time — then the cadence scans close the course.

outcomeSummary: Every important event written, collected in one place, and proven to arrive with its true source and time.
